morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with low branching habit and the female flower: a small annual often branching from the base, with sepals distinct to the base and broadest toward their tips; leaves lack the brown-dot effect of C. monanthogynus.
diagnostic_traits: annual monoecious herb, commonly low and dichotomously branched
leaves lanceolate to suborbiculate and not brown-dotted beneath
pistillate sepals usually 5–6, about 3 mm, tips incurved
three styles bifid to six terminal segments

confusers.separator: C. monanthogynus has dark-centered stellate hairs producing a brown-dotted lower leaf surface, two styles/four terminal segments, and a one-seeded fruit.
C. lindheimeri is generally more robust with acute leaves and much larger yellowish-woolly pistillate sepals.

abaxial leaf surface showing absence of brown-dot effect

morphology.look_here_first: Low/dichotomously branched annual with no brown-dot effect beneath the leaves; pistillate sepals about 3 mm and three bifid styles yielding six terminal segments.
morphology.key_separator: C. monanthogynus has dark-centered hairs, four terminal style branches and a one-seeded fruit; C. lindheimeri is more robust with larger yellowish-woolly pistillate sepals.
